alert: Database connection pool exhausted; payment API requests waiting for connections

2026-04-13T02:08:09Z pgbouncer-7f6c89c6d8-r7vnt LOG pool=payments cl_active=193 cl_waiting=87 sv_active=64
2026-04-13T02:08:15Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-p4mkr ERROR sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit reached, connection acquisition timed out

root_cause: The nightly batch consumed the available pgbouncer server pool and starved interactive application traffic of database connections.

actions.step: Scale payments-api replicas to reduce the request queue.
Raise PostgreSQL max_connections while the batch workload remains active.
Pause the nightly batch job and restart pgbouncer to clear the saturated pool.

postmortem: The scheduled batch consumed nearly all pooled database capacity and caused interactive requests to time out. More application replicas did not address the bottleneck; pausing the batch and restarting pgbouncer restored connection availability.

2026-04-15T06:25:04Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-x6mnr WARN cache_write_failures=63 fallback_reads=true
root_cause: The self-hosted Redis primary failed while loading its persisted dataset, leaving a healthy replica available for manual promotion.

actions.step: Restart Redis Sentinel and wait for it to complete failover.
Promote the healthy replica to primary using the manual failover procedure.
Update the Redis endpoint to the promoted primary and restart affected application pods.

postmortem: The primary could not recover its persisted dataset and stopped accepting normal traffic. Sentinel did not complete a usable automatic failover, so manual replica promotion and endpoint correction restored cache writes.

root_cause: An abandoned replication slot continued retaining WAL from a retired reporting consumer until the PostgreSQL volume became full.

postmortem: A retired replication slot retained a large WAL backlog and filled the PostgreSQL volume. Removing the abandoned slot released the retained WAL, and expanding storage provided additional safety margin.

root_cause: PayFlow response times increased beyond the five-second client deadline, producing a sustained series of upstream timeouts.

actions.step: Raise the PayFlow client timeout to twenty seconds.
Enable exponential backoff retries and activate the circuit breaker for PayFlow calls.
Fail over payment traffic to the secondary gateway.

postmortem: PayFlow latency exceeded the payments-api deadline and increased charge failures. Backoff and circuit protection reduced repeated pressure, while the secondary gateway could not accept the traffic during this event.
